program.name: 530A ("Trump") Accounts
program.description_short: $1,000 government investment account for U.S. citizen children born 2025-2028
program.description:
530A ("Trump") Accounts are special investment accounts for kids under 18. For children born between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2028, the government makes a one-time $1,000 deposit into the account. Children under 18 born outside this date range can still open an account — it just won't have the $1,000 deposit.

To open an account, a parent or guardian fills out IRS Form 4547. Any family can apply regardless of income, but the child must be a U.S. citizen with a Social Security Number. If your child does not yet have an SSN, apply at ssa.gov. Only one account is allowed per child.

The money is invested in index funds or ETFs, which are simple investments that follow the stock market (like the S&P 500). The law requires that these investments carry very low fees — no more than 0.10% per year.

A parent or guardian manages the account until the child turns 18. After that, withdrawals are allowed under traditional IRA rules (which say how and when withdrawals can be made).

Select 'Apply Online' to apply by signing into an IRS account and submitting Form 4547.
